hazards.name: Thunderstorm wind
hazards.frequency_note: about 19 a year reported in the county (568 in 1996-2026)

worst_local_event.summary: The Devens Fire Chief reported five injuries from Fort Devens when a military-grade tent was lifted up and blown down an embankment by thunderstorm winds.

hazards.name: High wind
hazards.frequency_note: about 12 a year reported in the county (358 in 1996-2026)

worst_local_event.summary: Sadly, winds gusting to around 50 mph, knocked down a rotted tree, which directly hit a 1-year-old baby, who his father was holding in the front yard of his house.

hazards.name: River flooding
hazards.frequency_note: about 6 a year reported in the county (183 in 1996-2026)

worst_local_event.summary: Each of the seven gaged mainstem rivers in Middlesex County rose above flood stage, the Nashua River at East Pepperell, Shawsheen River at Wilmington, and the Assabet River at Maynard all reached major flood.

hazards.name: Heavy snow
hazards.frequency_note: about 6.6 a year reported in the county (200 in 1996-2026)

worst_local_event.summary: An intense East Coast low pressure system moved northeast from eastern Georgia passing along the coast of the Carolinas and then close to 40 degrees North and 70 degrees West.

hazards.name: Hail
hazards.frequency_note: about 5.2 a year reported in the county (160 in 1996-2026)

worst_local_event.summary: Severe thunderstorms swept across western, central, and northeast Massachusetts and caused widespread damage.

hazards.name: Flash flood
hazards.frequency_note: about 2.5 a year reported in the county (75 in 1996-2026)

worst_local_event.summary: The most significant flash flooding affected Somerville, where damage was estimated to be around ten million dollars.

hazards.name: Lightning
hazards.frequency_note: about 2.1 a year reported in the county (63 in 1996-2026)

worst_local_event.summary: Severe thunderstorms brought damaging winds and hail to much of central and eastern Massachusetts.

hazards.name: Winter storm
hazards.frequency_note: about 2.8 a year reported in the county (84 in 1996-2026)

worst_local_event.summary: A total of 8-14 inches of snow fell across Western Middlesex County over the two day period.

hazards.name: Drought
hazards.frequency_note: about once a year reported in the county (30 in 1996-2026)

worst_local_event.summary: The U.S. Drought Monitor declared severe drought (D2) over northwest Middlesex County from April 12 through May 15.

hazards.name: Hurricane / tropical storm
hazards.frequency_note: about one every 5 years reported in the county (6 in 1996-2026)

worst_local_event.summary: Numerous trees were downed in Concord, two of these were downed onto houses.

hazards.name: Extreme heat
hazards.frequency_note: about one every 6 years reported in the county (5 in 1996-2026)

worst_local_event.summary: A 45 year old mail carrier died as a result of heat illness on July 6th.

hazards.name: Ice storm
hazards.frequency_note: about one every 8 years reported in the county (4 in 1996-2026)

worst_local_event.summary: Three-quarters of an inch of ice accumulated on exposed surfaces across northwest Middlesex County.

hazards.name: Extreme cold
hazards.frequency_note: about one every 8 years reported in the county (4 in 1996-2026)

worst_local_event.summary: The Automated Surface Observing System at Hanscom Field in Bedford, MA (KBED) recorded wind chills as low as 30 below zero.

hazards.name: Tornado
hazards.frequency_note: about one every 8 years reported in the county (4 in 1996-2026)

worst_local_event.summary: A tornado developed within an area of showers and thunderstorms moving through southern New England.

hazards.name: Earthquake
hazards.frequency_note: about a 0.2% chance in a given year (NRI)

notes: NRI ratings and frequencies are county-wide and compare the county with all US counties; they are not specific to the campus. NRI frequency units differ by hazard (events per year, event-days per year for heat, cold, drought and winter weather, annual probability for earthquake and wildfire). NRI Strong Wind, Winter Weather and Inland Flooding each cover two of our hazards, so the second one carries the rating only. Storm Events zone reports can cover a forecast zone larger than the county. Likelihood (chance of at least one event a year) and the order are computed by PARALLEL, not FEMA: from the local Storm Events rate when there is one, otherwise from NRI frequency capped at 0.5; ties go to the higher NRI rating. Storm Events: Middlesex County reports plus forecast zones MAZ005, MAZ014 (Southeast Middlesex, where Harvard is) and MAZ026. Storm Events 1996 through June 2026 (NCEI detail files, versions c2026xxxx); worst event = largest property+crop damage, with a death weighted as $10M and an injury as $1M.
